body:
## What

`getClientBrandForPreview()` gated on `requireAdminScope()`, which **throws for client/partner org-admins** — who, on the single-host model, are never `platform_admin`. Converts it to `resolveAuthorizedScope()` + the existing `assertCanManageBrandOwner('client', …)` helper.

## Why

This is the same recurring authorization bug that bit campaign branding (#311) and experience (#318): a **client-scoped** action reachable from tenant editors must gate on authority over the **client**, not platform-admin. `getClientBrandForPreview` is the one `brand.ts` read that #311 didn't convert.

It's **latent today** — the only caller is FlowEditor's "Preview as" client selector, which renders only when a `clients` prop is passed, and only the admin platform-experience editor (`(dashboard)/settings/experience`) passes it. The client/partner experience pages pass no `clients`, so the selector (and this call) never fire there. But it's a trap the moment a preview selector is surfaced in a tenant portal. Platform admins keep full access (`canManageClient` short-circuits on `isPlatformAdmin`); client org-admins can now preview their own client's brand.

Found during the follow-up audit of the `requireAdminScope`-throws-for-org-admins pattern (spawned from #311/#318). That audit otherwise cleared every campaign/client-scoped action — this was the sole remaining latent instance.

## Test

Adds `tests/integration/brand-preview-authz.test.ts` (fully mocked, no live DB — mirrors `email-template-actions.test.ts`), pinning:
- platform admin allowed (no regression to the admin preview flow),
- **client org-admin allowed** — the bug this closes,
- org-admin rejected for a client they don't manage, and non-admin rejected — with the gate short-circuiting before any brand lookup.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run tests/integration/brand-preview-authz.test.ts` → 4/4 pass
- `eslint` clean on changed files; `tsc` adds no new errors (only pre-existing `stripe` module-resolution errors remain)
- Architecture guards (`admin-actions-authz`, `integration-host-guard`) still pass

No DB/migration changes.

body:
## sc-9417 — sc-9089k: ltx packed-load (candle-gen-ltx) [HIGH]

Last crate of the **sc-9089** umbrella. Converts **candle-gen-ltx** (LTX-2.3 video: `AvDiT` video/audio DiT + Gemma-3-12B TE + connector + 3D-conv video VAE + audio VAE + vocoder) to the shared `candle_gen::quant` packed-load module (sc-9086), on the **flux2-dev template**.

### What changed
New per-crate **`quant.rs`**: `qlinear` / `qembedding` packed-**detect** via a `{key}.scales` sibling — build the quantized module straight from the MLX packed parts (Q4→`Q4_1` lossless, Q8→`Q8_0`) at the config group size (64, `PackedConfig`) by calling the shared loaders directly (`shared::QLinear::from_packed_gs` for Linears, `shared::embedding_gs` for `embed_tokens`). Routed through the whole **AvDiT attn/ff** + **Gemma** q/k/v/o/gate/up/down + `embed_tokens` + **connector** + **TE-projection** Linear surface. Forward **dequantizes-on-forward** into a dense matmul (sc-7702), never candle's int8 `QMatMul` fast path.

### Dense-path parity (qualified)
Absent `.scales`, the dense path is preserved, but parity is **not uniform** across the seam:
- **DiT / Gemma / connector Linear surface** (`qlinear`/`qembedding` dense arm): **byte-identical** to the legacy read — both cast to the bf16 DiT/Gemma builder dtype, a no-op.
- **VAE / audio-VAE / vocoder** (routed through `guard_no_scales`): the dense weight is cast to the passed builder dtype — **F32** for those builders — so a bf16 on-disk weight is **upcast to F32 (lossless)** where the pre-PR per-crate read kept the on-disk dtype. Values are preserved; the dtype is not necessarily byte-identical on disk.

### Per-component packed / dense split (hf-header audit of `SceneWorks/ltx-2.3-mlx` q4)
| Component | Packed surface |
|---|---|
| **AvDiT** `transformer.safetensors` | **PACKED** — 1344 `.scales`: `to_q/k/v/to_out` + `ff.proj_in/out` |
| Gemma-3-12B TE (`gemma/`) | dense in tier (0 `.scales`, no `quantization` block) |
| connector, video VAE (3D conv) enc/dec, audio VAE, vocoder, upsampler | dense (0 `.scales`) |

Only the AvDiT is packed in this tier. The 3D-conv VAEs, audio VAE and vocoder stay **dense**, loaded through **`guard_no_scales`** — errors loudly if a `.scales` sibling appears where a dense conv is expected (a tier that ever packs a conv would otherwise load u32 codes as garbage silently). `group_size` from config; `qlinear`/`qembedding` (linear/embedding-detect) everywhere.

### Shared-module reuse
Delegates to `candle_gen::quant::{QLinear::from_packed_gs, embedding_gs}`; `GROUP_SIZE` threaded; the local `QLinear`/`QEmbedding` are thin `Dense | Packed(shared::…)` wrappers, **not** a duplicate of the shared logic. Dense arm preserves the exact legacy bf16 read for the Linear surface.

### Tests (5, all green) — SYNTHETIC fixtures on the audited key layout
The wiring is validated with **synthetic** packed fixtures built on the **real** LTX AvDiT block-0 key layout the hf-header audit captured. These prove the packed-**detect** seam fires on that layout — **not** that a real tier was ingested or a real render run.
- `qlinear_packed_detect_on_avdit_key_layout` — packed-detect fires on the audited AvDiT block-0 key layout (`to_out` with no `.0`, dense `to_gate_logits`) with packed-vs-affine-grid parity (cosine > 0.99999). Confirms **not** a silent dense fallback.
- `qlinear_dense_path_unchanged` — dense arm byte-identical to the legacy read (max dev 0.0).
- `qembedding_packed_detect_on_gemma_embed_tokens` — fires on `embed_tokens.scales`, reproduces the grid.
- `packed_quantize_is_noop` — shared idempotent quantize no-op on a packed weight.
- `guard_no_scales_errors_on_packed_conv` — the VAE/vocoder guard.
- Full ltx lib suite: **23 passed**. `cargo fmt` + `clippy --all-targets` clean.
- **CUDA build on sm_120** (multi-arch fatbin, cap=80 baseline, VS2022 v143 + CUDA 12.9): `candle-gen-ltx --features cuda` + both examples **link**, EXIT=0.

### Deferred to sc-9545 — real tier ingestion + real packed render
No real packed render has been run in this PR. Two things are deferred to and tracked by **sc-9545**:
1. **Split-per-component tier ingestion** — the hosted `SceneWorks/ltx-2.3-mlx` tier ships one safetensors **per component** (not the crate's single bundled file), resolved from a `q4/`/`q8/` subfolder + `gemma/` shards, and its packed `transformer.safetensors` uses **different key names** than the dense Lightricks checkpoint the loaders assume (`to_out.0`↔`to_out`, `net.0.proj`/`net.2`↔`ff.proj_in/out`, `linear_1/2`↔`linear1/2`). The subfolder resolver + gemma shards + key remap are the ingestion effort.
2. **The real q4/q8 packed GPU video render** — blocked on (1).

The dense checkpoint (the only one the current loader resolves) needs ~68 GB of `Lightricks/LTX-2.3` + `gemma-3-12b-it` weights and exercises only the unchanged dense path.

**Audio chain:** the audio VAE + vocoder have **no packed tier** in the MLX snapshot (dense-only) — kept dense + guarded; no coverage faked.

Relates sc-9089. Epic 9083.

body:
Implements Wake-on-LAN end-to-end (#533): a magic-packet service plus three operator surfaces, with two vantages (control-plane server or a Fleet appliance on the target's L2 segment).

## What's included

**Backend service** (`app/services/wol.py`)
- `build_magic_packet` / `send_magic_packet` (102-byte AMD magic packet, MAC normalization, off-loop UDP broadcast).
- `WolWireRequest` / `WolResult` schemas + `resolve_wake_params` (IP → mac + subnet broadcast).
- Shared dispatch: `wake_from_server` / `wake_via_appliance` / `WolDispatchError` — one implementation used by every entrypoint.

**Surfaces**
- **IP detail modal** — a **Wake** button, shown only when the IP has a MAC; resolves MAC + subnet broadcast server-side. `POST /ipam/addresses/{id}/wake`.
- **Network Tools page** — a MAC-based **Wake-on-LAN** tool (MAC + optional broadcast + port + server/appliance vantage). `POST /tools/wol`.
- **Operator Copilot** — `propose_wake_host` (propose → Apply flow, like `propose_run_nmap_scan`).

**Appliance vantage** — a `wol` runner added to the supervisor's nettool executor (`agent/supervisor/.../nettools.py`) so the packet originates on the target's segment, reusing the existing generic nettool command channel (no new transport).

**Cross-cutting** — gated `read:use_network_tools` (matches the rest of the network-tools surface), audited (`action="wake_on_lan"`) at every entrypoint. WoL is IPv4-only (the magic packet rides a UDP broadcast). No new migration, permission, or feature module.

## Self-review

Ran `/code-review` at high effort; the 6 real findings are all fixed in `e6c2b2c` + `c43fec9`:
- permission action `write` → `read` (parity with ping/nmap/dig),
- server-vantage `OSError` → clean 502 (was a raw 500),
- `WakeHostArgs.port` bounds,
- **de-duplicated** the IP→(mac,broadcast) resolution and the appliance-dispatch/error-mapping into the shared `wol` service,
- appliance dispatch timeout 15s → 30s,
- frontend renders `detail` only when it's a string (a Pydantic 422 detail is a list).

## Verification

ruff / black / mypy on all changed backend + agent files; eslint (`--max-warnings 0`) / prettier / `tsc -b` + vite build on frontend; app boots with both routes live (`/api/v1/ipam/addresses/{id}/wake`, `/api/v1/tools/wol`) and `wake_host` registered at `read:use_network_tools`. Exercised end-to-end against the local Docker stack.

Closes #533

body:
## Summary

Full remediation of the findings from a four-track architecture/correctness review, executed as reviewed phases with mutation-checked regression tests throughout (plans: `impl-plan/0015-review-remediation.md`, `impl-plan/0016-typescript-remediation.md`).

### Rust (9 phases)
- **Replay correctness**: command matching no longer falsely reports nondeterminism on out-of-order ready events (reproduced bug); one signal delivery resolves exactly one waiter; terminal states with un-replayed command events fail as divergence.
- **Crash safety**: workflow/activity claims carry lease expiry with token-bumped fencing; worker error paths release claims and recovery slots; timeout-less activities use the lease as an implicit heartbeat interval (heartbeating holders survive indefinitely).
- **Provider unification**: terminal guard, ready-reason resolution, retry/timeout decisions, child mappings, and persisted codecs are shared pure functions; the Postgres lost-signal-wakeup race is closed in both commit paths.
- **Payload safety**: GC min-age grace period with delete-time re-probe; URI scheme ownership inverted (custom blob stores work); inline manifest roots hydrate blob pages; commit path stops downloading blobs to validate refs.
- **Simulation**: the harness drives the real Worker over MemoryBackend with seeded fault injection; the crash scenario provably catches the lease fix's absence.
- **Performance** (Criterion vs saved baselines): held-handle −64.6%, Postgres child wakeup −33.7%, commit −25.1%, history stream −24.9% (O(N²) transfer fixed), SQLite claim/complete −17.9%; write-only shard journal removed; terminal rows deleted. Mixed workloads: SQLite +10%, Postgres +24.7%, 100-shard +126%.
- **Production worker**: `Worker::run()` with graceful shutdown, `wait_for_ready` backend hook, real bounded activity concurrency, bounded LRU cache.
- **Packaging/API honesty**: provider feature gates (default tree 458→84 crates), benchtools workspace split, real exponential retry backoff, strict-mode compile error, manifest hash renames, count-only select digest (breaking history change, recorded).

### TypeScript (2 phases)
- GC min-age grace period (upload-race closed); heartbeats renew the claim lease (no more deterministic duplicate execution past 30s); terminal divergence check; backend `releaseWorkflowTask` with full worker error-path wiring and batch drain; foreign-scheme hydration pass-through; shared terminal-commit guard. Mixed workloads: SQLite +10–15%, memory +4.4%; the apparent Postgres regression was proven to be a stale baseline (bisect + statement profiling in the 0016 ledger).

### Versioning
`durust` and `durust-macros` bump 0.1.2 → 0.2.0 (breaking: Postgres schema v6, select-digest history break, manifest field renames, feature-gated providers).

## Test plan
- [x] Rust: full workspace suite green with all features + Postgres fixture (85 lib / 47 conformance / 118 replay / 7 sim / 4 worker_run); fmt + feature matrix clean
- [x] TS: `npm run check` green (399 tests); Postgres conformance 95 + thresholds 14 against the fixture
- [x] Every phase reviewer-approved; every fix mutation-checked
- [x] Benchmarks documented in both READMEs with reproduction commands

body:
Addresses #93.

## Summary

Adds `scripts/e2e_demo.py`, an orchestrator that drives **one task through the 4 hops MAP → RECALL → EDIT → VERIFY** and writes a `simplicio.savings-event/v1`-shaped receipt per hop (`proof.kind` + fixed `ceil(chars/4)` tokenizer labeled on every number — never a bare percentage). It reuses `savings_harness.py`'s snapshot store, so `savings_harness.py score` and `billing_aggregator.py collect`/`meter` pick these hops up automatically — no new aggregation code.

```bash
python3 scripts/e2e_demo.py run         # live demo against a real repo
python3 scripts/e2e_demo.py selftest    # offline, no external tools — what scripts/check.py runs
```

Registered as a worker selftest in `scripts/claims_audit.py` (`SELFTEST_SCRIPTS`) and `tests/test_worker_selftests.py`, and documented in `README.md` under a new "e2e savings demo" subsection.

## Scope note

#93 is explicitly a capstone/acceptance-test issue for a program with **three upstream cross-repo dependencies that are not live in this environment**:

- `simplicio-mapper#148/#149` (native `--for-llm toon` on `handoff`) — not in the installed `simplicio-mapper` (checked the CLI help; no such flag).
- `simplicio-dev-cli#88` (`SIMPLICIO_PROMPT_TOON=1` + TOON rows in `.simplicio/runs.jsonl`) — not in the installed `simplicio-cli` (checked the package source; no reference).
- `simplicio-runtime#2774/#2775` (`simplicio memory`, `auto_meter`, the authoritative `simplicio.savings-event/v1` envelope) — the `simplicio` runtime binary isn't installed at all in this sandbox.

Given that, this PR implements the **best real first slice**, not a full close of every AC:

- **MAP** and **VERIFY** hops are **100% live**: real `simplicio-mapper handoff <repo> --json` output TOON-encoded with this repo's own `toon_codec.py`, and real `task_anchor.py check --format json` vs `--format toon` against the same anchored verdict (task_anchor already supported `--format toon` before this PR — nothing new needed there).
- **RECALL** substitutes the mapper's already-fetched compact per-file index for the unavailable `simplicio memory` call (raw file reads vs compact index, budget-capped at 2048 chars per the issue). Labeled explicitly in the event's `note`.
- **EDIT** calls the REAL `simplicio.prompt.build_prompt()` in-process (genuine current dev-cli prompt text, no LLM call, no API key) as the baseline, and TOON-encodes the same structured context fields as an honest local stand-in for the not-yet-shipped `SIMPLICIO_PROMPT_TOON` flag — per AC5's explicit allowance for "mocks/local onde preciso, honestamente rotulado". I also confirmed by reading `pipeline.run_task` that even `--dry-run-task` calls the LLM provider, so a genuinely live dev-cli A/B needs `SIMPLICIO_MODEL`+key regardless of dev-cli#88's status, and can't run in AC5's keyless CI gate either way.
- The **VERIFY** hop intentionally leaves AC4 (the live dev-cli A/B) marked `partial` in its own demo anchor, so `task_anchor.py gate` correctly reports `blocked` — proof the gate isn't a rubber stamp, and an honest reflection that AC4 isn't fully closed by this PR.
- The `simplicio.savings-event/v1` schema used here is a **local, explicitly-labeled subset** (`profile: simplicio-loop.e2e-demo/v1`) — while building this I found live example records of that schema already circulating in this shared sandbox's `~/.simplicio/ledger/savings-events.jsonl` (from concurrent runtime#2774/#2775 test activity), which gave me real field names to align with, but I did not treat those as the merged/final spec since I haven't seen the actual spec issue.

**A genuinely new, unrelated finding surfaced while building this** (documented in the script's module docstring, not fixed here — out of scope): `simplicio-mapper macro` returned file paths from an entirely different, unrelated project (`/home/user/hermes-turbo-agent`) when run against this repo, apparently via a shared, weakly-scoped `~/.simplicio/cache/` on this multi-tenant sandbox. `handoff`/`inspect` were verified clean via a control run in an isolated empty directory, so this script only ever calls those two verbs, plus a sanity check that rejects any returned path outside the repo before trusting it. Worth a follow-up issue on `simplicio-mapper`.

## What's NOT done

- No live A/B against `simplicio-dev-cli`'s actual `SIMPLICIO_PROMPT_TOON` toggle (doesn't exist yet upstream).
- No integration with the real `simplicio-runtime` `auto_meter`/`simplicio memory` (binary not installed here).
- The full canonical `simplicio.savings-event/v1` envelope (user/team/actor/llm/cost/privacy fields) is not reproduced — only a local, honestly-labeled subset relevant to this repo's model-free workers.

## Validation

```
python3 scripts/e2e_demo.py selftest      # PASS 15/15
python3 scripts/e2e_demo.py run           # live: MAP/RECALL/EDIT/VERIFY all produced real receipts
python3 scripts/savings_harness.py score  # picks up the 3 token-count hops automatically
python3 scripts/billing_aggregator.py collect && ... meter --json   # rolls up tokens_spent/saved
python3 scripts/check.py                  # claims-audit: 7/7 PASS; pytest: 180 passed, 1 pre-existing
                                           # failure unrelated to this change (see below)
```

`scripts/check.py` has **one pre-existing test failure** unrelated to this change:
`tests/test_loop_e2e.py::test_bound_operator_missing_blocks_when_simplicio_loop_shipped` — that test assumes `simplicio-mapper`/`simplicio-dev-cli` are NOT installed in the test sandbox, but this particular environment has both installed system-wide (I used them for real, live hops above), so the "missing bound operator" precondition doesn't hold here. Confirmed by stashing this PR's changes and re-running the same test against unmodified `main` — it fails identically. Not touched by this diff.

## Files

- `scripts/e2e_demo.py` (new)
- `scripts/claims_audit.py` — registered `scripts/e2e_demo.py` in `SELFTEST_SCRIPTS`
- `tests/test_worker_selftests.py` — added `test_e2e_demo_selftest`

body:
Wave 1 of the feature roadmap — ideas **1** ("feels like") and **5** (sun times), bundled as planned. Both are pure derived data: no new fetch, no new dependency, no new KV key, and no meaningful page-weight increase. Two commits, one per feature.

## Commit 1 — "feels like" temperature (heat index / wind chill)

Computed in-Worker from data NWS already gives us (`temperature`, `relativeHumidity`, `windSpeed`), using NWS's own published formulas (Rothfusz regression; NWS wind chill equation).

- **`feelsLikeRawF(period)`** — unconditional value (heat index at ≥80°F, wind chill at ≤50°F + wind ≥3 mph, else `null`). Feeds `/api/weather` (new `feelsLike` on `current` + each `hourly` entry) and the `/hourly` "Feels"/"Sensación" column ("–" when N/A).
- **`feelsLikeF(period)`** — gated to ≥3°F difference from air temp for prominent single-value spots: homepage hero, homepage markdown, MCP `get_current_conditions` text.
- `/about` (EN + ES) honesty note; OpenAPI documents the field as computed, not raw NWS.

## Commit 2 — sunrise/sunset times

Standard astronomical sunrise equation (SunCalc formulation) — the NWS forecast API doesn't provide sun times.

- Homepage hero + markdown: today's sunrise/sunset (EN "Sunrise/Sunset", ES "Amanecer/Atardecer").
- `/hourly` (HTML + markdown): per-day sun times in each day heading.
- `/api/weather`: new `sun.sunrise`/`sun.sunset` (ISO, documented in OpenAPI); MCP `get_current_conditions` text + `structuredContent`.
- `sunTimesForCtDate()` anchors computation to noon Central of the timestamp's own calendar date, so evening hours can't round into the next solar day (explicitly tested).
- `/about` note extended to cover both derived values; CLAUDE.md derived-data convention updated.

## Verification

Formula validation **before** wiring, both features:
- **Heat index / wind chill** validated against published NWS chart reference values — this caught a real transcription bug (Rothfusz coefficient off by 1000×, producing five-digit heat indexes) before it ever reached a render path. Fixed; all reference points within 1°F (the regression's own error bound is ±1.3°F).
- **Sun times** validated against published Houston-area sunrise/sunset for summer, winter, and both equinoxes — all within ~2 min, day lengths correct (including >12h equinox days from refraction), and the evening-hour day-snapping edge case covered.

End-to-end against `wrangler dev --local` with live Crosby data: hero (EN + ES), homepage markdown, `/hourly` HTML + markdown, `/api/weather`, OpenAPI, MCP tool text + structuredContent, `/about` copy — all render correctly. Edge cases: cold-snap wind chill, missing `relativeHumidity`, `null` period, neutral 51–79°F range (suppressed, no crash). Full route regression sweep (17 routes, EN + ES) — all 200. `node --check` passes.

author: kfox
body:
## Summary

Bumps the default `[audio].sample_rate` (the 4-bit/8-bit `$D418` NMI-DAC path) from **11600 → 12000 Hz**, lifting the Nyquist to ~6.0 kHz so fricatives/sibilants survive with clearer speech. Backed by a full-pipeline pitch A/B sweep on real NTSC hardware.

## Why 12000

The isolated NMI-handler cycle budget in `c64.py` (~13.6 kHz NTSC) was measured with a *prefilled* ring and no host feed. Under the **live streaming pipeline**, the host-DMA audio-ring writes themselves halt the 6510 and steal handler cycles, so overrun onsets lower.

A new full-pipeline sweep (`scripts/diags/nmi_rate_sweep_ab.py`) plays the same clip at a range of rates and reads the *played* pitch by log-spectrum cross-correlation against the source — a rate whose pitch drops below the low-rate floor is the NMI handler queuing. Measured onset **~12.5 kHz**:

| Rate | petscii | mhires | verdict |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| 11600 | +0.11% | +0.13% | clean floor |
| 12000 | +0.19% | +0.19% | **clean floor (chosen)** |
| 13000 | −0.55% | −0.46% | overrun onset |
| 13500 | −0.40% | −0.38% | overrun |
| 15000 | −1.23% | −1.14% | clear overrun (positive control) |

The onset is **identical in char and bitmap modes**, so the driver is the host-DMA audio feed (not the video bus load). 12000 is the highest rate on the clean floor with margin below the onset.

Sample rate (Nyquist) is orthogonal to the `$D418` bit depth (`dac_curve`): the NMI handler is the same 32-byte ring-byte→`$D418` routine for the 4-bit linear and 8-bit Mahoney curves, so this ceiling holds for both. The sweep and final verification both ran on the shipped **8-bit Mahoney** default (`dac_curve = "auto"`).

## Verification

End-to-end at the shipped default (no rate override): DAC path, petscii, speech clip → **+0.04% pitch, no underruns**, speech clear and comprehensible.

`make` gates: mypy --strict + pyright clean, 1745 tests pass, schema regenerated (drift tests green).

## Changes

- `config.py`: default 11600 → 12000 + refreshed help (documents the live-pipeline onset vs the isolated-handler ceiling).
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/usage.md`, `config/c64cast.example.toml`; `c64cast.schema.json` regenerated; default-rate test updated.
- New reusable diag tools: `nmi_rate_sweep_ab.py` (the rate A/B) and `capture_fidelity_probe.py` (a sampler click-train probe, staged for a separate follow-up).

author: romthpt
body:
Found by a byte-exact oracle sweep against live mainnet: an `AMMWithdraw`
with `tfWithdrawAll` on a pool with **more than one liquidity provider**
diverged from rippled (7/8 affected nodes mismatched on mainnet ledger
105322820).

## Root cause
`equal_withdraw_tokens` always snapped the burned LP tokens onto the pool's
LP grid via `adjust_lp_tokens_withdraw`, even for `tfWithdrawAll`. rippled's
`adjustLPTokensIn` only does that for a **partial** (`LPTokenIn`) withdraw —
for `withdrawAll` it returns the requested tokens **unadjusted**:

```cpp
adjustLPTokensIn(rules, lptAMMBalance, lpTokensWithdraw, withdrawAll) {
    if (!rules.enabled(fixAMMv1_3) || withdrawAll == WithdrawAll::Yes)
        return lpTokensWithdraw;              // full balance, no rounding
    return adjustLPTokens(lptAMMBalance, lpTokensWithdraw, IsDeposit::No);
}
```

For a holder that is not the sole LP, the rounding left a **dust LP balance**,
so `finish_withdraw` saw `remaining != 0` and kept the LP trust line instead
of deleting it — diverging both owner directories, the account `OwnerCount`
(14 vs 13), and shifting the pool balances / `LPTokenBalance` by 1 ULP.

## Fix
In the non-drains-all branch of `equal_withdraw_tokens`, use the holder's
balance directly when `withdraw_all` is set (no grid adjustment), so the
line drains to zero and is deleted. One-line behavioural change, gated on
`withdraw_all`.

## Verification
- `AMMWithdraw tfWithdrawAll` (mainnet L105322820): **7 → 0 mismatches**.
- No regression: `AMMDeposit` and partial `AMMWithdraw` oracles still 0
  mismatches; 544 tx-engine tests green; clippy clean.

body:
## Bug

The admin GUI runs as **root** (via polkit), so a settings file exported from it was written **root-owned with `0600`**. The user's own apps (file manager, Google Drive uploader) run as the normal user and can't read a root-owned locked file → uploading it failed with a permission/"can't read the file" error.

## Fix

`export_settings` now hands the finished file to the human who launched the app, resolved from **`PKEXEC_UID` / `SUDO_UID`**, via `os.chown`. It stays `0600`, so it's still **private to that user** (not world-readable) — but now readable/movable by them. Non-root exports are unaffected.

Added `_invoking_user_ids()` helper.

## Testing
- `_invoking_user_ids()` resolves `PKEXEC_UID`/`SUDO_UID` to (uid, gid) and returns None when unset.
- `python3 -m py_compile appblocker.py` passes.

## Note
App-code only. Also works for the CLI `--export-settings` under `sudo`. Users with an already-exported (root-owned) file can fix it in place with `sudo chown $USER: <file>` without waiting for the update.

body:
## 1. IMU pointing: rotation-rate gate (replaces displacement-since-solve)
The v0.11.9 displacement gate cured parked gyro drift but froze the crosshair for **slow pans** too — each solve re-anchors the reference, so sub-1°/solve motion never engaged and rendered as solve-rate steps. The gyro knows the difference directly: parked drift is ~0.01°/s, even a slow manual nudge is >0.1°/s.

- New `imu_rate_gate_dps` (default **0.1°/s**, config + `shared_cfg`), measured over a ≥0.8 s baseline of poll-time samples (short windows would let quantization noise swamp slow pans).
- **Hold-until-re-anchor:** once engaged, the prediction holds after motion stops until a fresh solve lands — so stopping never snaps the crosshair back by the whole slew distance; the hand-back to the solved fix is seamless.

author: adhithyan15
body:
## Summary

The `deflate` crate's `compress`/`decompress` used a **non-standard custom container** — a 4-byte length prefix, an explicit `(symbol, code_length)` table, and a private bit stream — that *no other tool could read*. This makes it standard: `compress` now emits a **standard RFC 1951 raw DEFLATE stream** (the same bytes a ZIP entry or gzip body carries), and `decompress` becomes an alias for the hardened `inflate`.

This is the natural companion to the OOXML M0 work: the decoder already reads real-world DEFLATE; now the encoder *writes* it.

## What ships

- **`compress` → standard RFC 1951.** Emits a single **fixed-Huffman block** (BTYPE=01) using the pre-defined code tables of RFC 1951 §3.2.6, so no table is transmitted. Decodable by any conforming inflater — our `inflate`, `zlib`, `gzip`, `unzip`, browsers. LZSS window widened to the full **32768**.
- **`decompress` → `inflate`.** The custom-format decoder (with its unchecked indexing, back-reference-offset underflow, and no output cap — flagged as latent bugs during the M0 review) is **deleted**; `decompress` forwards to the hardened, 256 MB-bomb-capped `inflate`, which reads stored/fixed/dynamic blocks. No caller outside the crate used `compress`/`decompress`.
- **Removed:** the custom-format machinery (`build_canonical_codes`, `reverse_code_map`, `unpack_bits`, `write_bit_string`, the `HuffmanTree` encoder) and the **`huffman-tree` dependency** (fixed Huffman needs no tree construction).
- **Docs:** module doc, `CMP05-deflate.md` spec (wire format, encode/decode algorithms, constant tables, test vectors), and CHANGELOG all updated to the standard format. **Net −500 lines.**

## Standard-conformance — verified both directions

- Our `inflate` decodes a real **Python-`zlib`** raw stream (existing test from M0).
- **Python's `zlib.decompress(compress(x), wbits=-15)`** decodes our output back to `x` — checked for empty, literal-only, and match-bearing inputs.
- In-crate `roundtrip` now also asserts `inflate(compress(x)) == x` and that the stream starts with a valid fixed-Huffman block header.

## Test plan

- [x] `deflate` — 23 tests pass (roundtrip + standard-decode + header checks)
- [x] `png` (downstream, uses `zlib_compress`/`zlib_decompress` — unchanged) — 15 pass
- [x] `zip` (downstream) — 24 lib + 5 doc pass
- [x] No compiler warnings
- [x] Security review passed (encoder panic-freedom, no underflow, `decompress→inflate` removes risk)

## Notes

- **Breaking wire-format change** (0.2.1 → **0.3.0**): old custom-format bytes are no longer produced or parsed. Nothing is released and no external caller used the custom `compress`/`decompress`.
- Fixed Huffman is standard and correct for every input but not the smallest encoding. **Dynamic-Huffman encoding** (BTYPE=10, better ratios) is a queued follow-up; it needs length-limited Huffman trees. The decoder already reads dynamic blocks.

body:
## Summary

Two SeedSigner screen items surfaced while exercising the ESP32-P4 build, plus a couple of forward-looking TODO notes.

### 1. `fix(mnemonic)`: defer the candidate list until a 2nd letter; blank touch keyboard
The touch candidate panel rebuilt one LVGL widget per matching word on **every** keystroke. A single letter matches up to ~250 BIP-39 words, so the very first keystroke stalled slower displays (notably the ESP32-P4) for a visible beat — and a 1-letter candidate list has little practical value.

- The on-screen candidate panel (and its accept affordances) now wait for a 2-letter prefix (`MNEMONIC_MATCH_MIN_LETTERS` / `mnemonic_matches_shown()`). `possible_words` is still computed at every stage — the keyboard's next-letter dimming derives from it — so only the *panel* is deferred, not the matching. Gated in four places: the hardware fixed-slot panel, the touch list, KEY1/KEY3 scroll, and KEY2 accept (so an off-screen candidate can't be accepted).
- The touch keyboard now starts **blank**: the pre-highlighted letter is a joystick-cursor affordance, so the buttonmatrix selection is explicitly cleared to `LV_BUTTONMATRIX_BUTTON_NONE` in touch mode (hardware still installs the cursor). Mirrors `button_list_screen`, where initial selection is hardware-mode only.

### 2. `feat(seed)`: `seed_finalize_screen` — the fingerprint step after a seed is loaded
Ports Python's `SeedFinalizeScreen`: a bottom-pinned button list (Done / BIP-39 Passphrase, no back button) whose one special element is a centered fingerprint readout — the master-fingerprint hex under a small "fingerprint" label, beside a large blue fingerprint icon.

- Layout is derived directly from Python's `IconTextLine(is_text_centered=True, icon_name=FINGERPRINT)`: a horizontally-centered `[icon][gap][label-over-value]` group, icon vertically centered against the two-line block, whole group vertically centered between the top-nav and the first button.
- Adds `INFO_COLOR` (#409CFF) and `seedsigner_latin_font()`, a memoized regular-weight Latin (OpenSans) font at an arbitrary body-relative size — used for the always-Latin hex value at an exact body+2 (19px). The translatable "fingerprint" label uses the locale-aware `BODY_FONT` (see TODO below).
- Registered in both desktop tool registries; adds a `seed_finalize_screen` scenario (+ a `no_passphrase` variant).

Rendered output matches the Python reference across resolutions:

| Python reference (240×240) | This PR (240×240) |
|---|---|
| `SeedFinalizeView` | title + centered fingerprint icon/label/value + Done (selected) / BIP-39 Passphrase |

### 3. `docs(todo)`: two follow-ups
- **Locale-aware body-2 (label) font role** — the fingerprint label falls back to `BODY_FONT` (17px) because there's no locale-aware body-2 (15px) role yet; add one so `IconTextLine` labels match Python across locales.
- **Camera entropy overlay screen(s)** — not yet defined; the "new seed from camera entropy" flow needs its own live-preview overlay, to be designed in coordination with the ESP32 camera pipeline and the Pi Zero camera backend.

## Testing
- Built the desktop screenshot generator; rendered all scenarios at 240×240 / 320×240 / 480×320 / 800×480.
- `seed_finalize_screen` (+ `no_passphrase`) matches the Python reference.
- Mnemonic: verified 1-letter → no candidate panel; 2-letter ("mu") → candidates render as before; touch keyboard starts blank; hardware keyboard keeps the joystick cursor.

## Note (not in this repo)
The ESP32-P4 dice-roll keyboard showed blank FA dice glyphs. That is **not** a screens bug — the dice glyphs are baked into the icon font at every size and `keyboard_screen` renders them when `keyboard_font: "icon"` is set (verified on desktop). The caller (per-platform binding pass-through) must pass that flag; coordination notes were added in the two platform repos.

Opening Settings crashed with an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` in
`ListPreference.getEntry()` on locales whose translated `*_entries` arrays
hold fewer items than the matching `entryValues` arrays. At 4.5.2 this affects:

- `values-es-rMX` — ships `fontSize_entries` with 1 of 3 items
- `values-ast`, `values-oc`, `values-pt-rPT` — ship `darkmode_entries` with 2 of 3 items

author: josh-sea
body:
## What

One-line fix for the last auto-deploy blocker: scope the CI deploy to `--only hosting,firestore:rules` instead of `--only hosting,firestore`.

## Why

Run #1 (after the IAM role fix) got all the way to Firestore and stopped on:

```
firestore: there are 5 indexes defined in your project that are not present in your firestore indexes file.
Error: Pass the --force flag to use this command in non-interactive mode
```

The Firebase project has 5 indexes (created outside this repo) that `firestore.indexes.json` doesn't list. In non-interactive CI, firebase-tools requires `--force` to proceed — and `--force` **deletes those production indexes**. Skipping index deployment is the safe call: rules (which CanITwo needs) and hosting still deploy on every merge; indexes stay managed in the Firebase console.

To re-enable index deploys later: run `firebase firestore:indexes > firestore.indexes.json` locally to sync the file with production, commit it, and change the deploy flag back to `--only hosting,firestore`. (Notes are in the workflow header comment.)

## Effect

Merging this PR triggers the workflow with the fix already in place, so the merge itself should complete the first successful auto-deploy: hosting + the CanITwo Firestore rules go live.

author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
## Summary

#122 was squash-merged (`e49d143`) **before** the fix commit `1b34213` landed, so current `master` is missing that fix. This PR applies the stranded fix onto current master. It contains one real bug fix plus behavior-preserving restructures that let the hard JET `test_package` check run on all lanes.

### The real bug

`src/euler/euler.jl` — the inplace Hermite-interpolation branch read `length(u)` **before** `u` was ever assigned (a guaranteed `UndefVarError` on that path) and looped pointlessly reassigning a whole broadcast. Rewritten to match the `rk4`/`tsit5` siblings: allocate `u = similar(y₁)` first, then fill element-wise with the same linear interpolant the out-of-place branch returns (`(1 - Θ)*y₀ + Θ*y₁`).

Verified on Julia 1.12 that the old code throws `UndefVarError: u not defined in local scope`, and the fixed code returns the correct linear interpolant.

### JET false-positive restructures (behavior-preserving)

- **`cur_t` hoist** — in `atsit5.jl __solve`, `gpuatsit5.jl`, `gpuvern7.jl`, `gpuvern9.jl`: hoist the `cur_t = 1` initializer above the `saveat` if/else so it is unconditionally defined. It is read only when `saveat !== nothing`, and the else branch already re-established it, so runtime behavior is unchanged; JET can now prove it defined.
- **`q11` hoist** — in the adaptive `step!` methods (`atsit5.jl` ×5) and the `gpuatsit5`/`gpuvern7`/`gpuvern9` error-estimate blocks: compute `@fastmath q11 = EEst^beta1` before the `iszero(EEst)` guard. `q11` is read only when `EEst > 1` (which implies `EEst != 0`), and when `iszero(EEst)` the value is never used, so this is behavior-preserving; JET can now prove it defined.

### QA marker drop

`test/qa/qa.jl` — drop `const jet_broken = VERSION >= v"1.12"` and the `jet_broken` kwarg, leaving a plain `run_qa(SimpleDiffEq; explicit_imports = true)`. The hard `test_package` JET check now runs on all lanes.

## Verification (run locally)

- **JET on Julia 1.12.6 (JET 0.11.5):** `report_package(SimpleDiffEq; mode = :typo, target_defined_modules = true)` returns **0 reports** (was 36).
- **Euler inplace interpolation path:** returns the correct linear interpolant, no `UndefVarError`.
- **Core group on Julia 1.10:** all test files pass (`SimpleDiffEq tests passed`), incl. the adaptive `step!`, saveat interpolation, and GPU solve paths that were restructured (only the 1 pre-existing `@test_broken` in `discrete_tests.jl` remains broken).

author: malpern
body:
## Summary

Closes the fresh-install **Input Monitoring dead-end** on macOS 26/27 — the spot where the 2026-07-02 QA session "effectively died" (#931). #937 already fixed KeyPath.app's own IM *signal* (`IOHIDCheckAccess`); this fixes the wizard **UX** that was still stranded, plus a root-cause polling-lifecycle bug that would have defeated the fix.

### The problem
Clicking **Turn On** fires `IOHIDRequestAccess`, but on macOS 26/27 tccd can produce **no prompt and no TCC row** — the app never appears in the Input Monitoring list. The page kept showing only a bare "Turn On" button that deep-links to a Settings row which doesn't exist, giving the user no accurate way forward.

### The fix
- **Pure, unit-tested resolver** (`InputMonitoringGuidance`, in `KeyPathWizardCore`) that escalates KeyPath.app's own IM guidance: offer the automatic prompt first, then after a short wait window without a grant switch to explicit manual **"+"-to-add** steps. A `nil` or negative (clock-rewind) elapsed escalates rather than stranding the user in an endless "waiting" state.
- **`InputMonitoringManualFallbackCard`** rendered from that state, so the page never sits unresolved without accurate manual instructions — satisfying the #931 acceptance criterion ("never sits at `unknown` indefinitely without guidance").

### Root-cause polling fix (caught in review)
The escalation relies on periodic re-renders driven by the 1s `permissionSnapshot` poll. But the fast post-prompt poll (`startPermissionPolling`) **cancelled** the durable 1s poll, **stopped writing** `permissionSnapshot`, and **never restarted** it — so after ~5s the page went static: no re-renders (the card could never appear) and no detection of a later *manual* grant (the wizard could never advance). Fixed by extracting a durable `startBackgroundPermissionPolling()`, having the fast poll also refresh the snapshot, and resuming the durable poll when the fast poll exhausts.

## Testing
- New `InputMonitoringGuidanceTests` cover every resolver transition, the wait-window boundary, and the `nil`/negative-elapsed escalation guards.
- ⚠️ Swift build, full `swift test`, `swiftformat`, and `swiftlint` **were not run** here — this change was authored in a Linux container with no Swift/macOS toolchain. Please run the pre-PR gate on macOS.
- Manual first-run QA (#747) still required on a Mac without pre-granted permissions, ideally on a macOS 26 and a macOS 27 machine.

## Scope / follow-ups
Deliberately scoped to the KeyPath.app IM escalation. Still open on #931 and tracked separately:
- kanata-launcher self-registration / daemon-before-IM-step (#931)
- Welcome intro page (#932), drag-to-authorize parity + FDA polling (#933), wizard polish batch (#934)

## Review gate
CLAUDE.md's mandated `/thermo-nuclear-swift-review` command isn't present in this checkout, so the built-in `/code-review` (high effort) was run against the diff instead; all confirmed findings — the fatal dead-poll bug, the clock-rewind edge, and the design-token/comment drift — were addressed.

author: awskii
body:
Three correctness bugs in the parallel/streaming commitment deep fold (gated behind `--experimental.parallel-commitment` / `--experimental.streaming-commitment`, default off). On affected inputs each yields a wrong state root, a corrupted persisted branch, or a panic. All reproduced red-first and verified against the sequential trie (root + stored-branch parity).

## Changes
- `updateCell` clears a reused cell's stale storage plain key when stamping an account key, so an injected deep-fold storage root is not shadowed by the stale slot in `computeCellHash`.
- `aggregateMountedStorageRoot` builds the storage root for a single-surviving-child collapse directly at the account boundary. The old `base.fold()` prepended the 64-nibble account prefix, overflowing `cell.extension` (panic) or returning the child hash instead of the extension hash (all-zero / wrong root).
- Mount split: `seedRootBase` seeds a row-0 wall so `foldMounted` always excludes the mount nibble; the `stitchSplitCells` strip is removed and the no-wall fallback becomes a hard error. Fixes an over-strip of extension-topped cells that corrupted the persisted branch and diverged the next block.

No change to the default single-trie commitment path.

body:
## What & why

The Groove protocol was defined twice, incompatibly: this repo (the substance — spec, working CLI, Zig reference, papers) and the newer `groove` repo (which *declared* itself canonical but was ~95% empty template with a 119-line sketch that contradicted this spec on transport, lifecycle, and licensing). This PR makes `groove-protocol` the single canonical home, adds the "it actually works" vertical slice the project never had, and kills the contradictory-port-table and license-drift problem classes.

Decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/decisions/` (0001–0008); any can be revisited before merge.

## Key changes

- **Consolidation (ADR 0001).** Absorbed `groove`'s real content: the cleave-layering design → `spec/LAYERING.adoc` (explicitly **aspirational annex**, not normative); the relocated gossamer Idris2 proofs → `proofs/` (honest README: not yet decoupled/typechecked, task PROOFS-1); the historical S-expr manifest → `docs/archive/`.
- **Spec truth pass (ADR 0002/0003).** `SPEC.adoc` v0.2.0-draft adds the manifest-encoding model — `application/groove+json` REQUIRED (the dialect the code actually implements), `application/groove+a2ml` optional/serve-only (no parser exists in scope). `CONFORMANCE.adoc` rewritten as an executable checklist (CONF-L1-01..04, CONF-L2-01..07); former L3/L4 moved to an aspirational annex. `IPV6T.adoc` header size corrected 105 → 108 (matches the Zig code + its passing tests). `READINESS.md` rewritten honestly (removed the fictional architecture tree and "65+ repos" claims).
- **Single port registry (ADR 0006).** `registry/groove-registry.json` is now the one source of truth; the CLI embeds it at compile time, the extension's port table is generated from it, and `cli/tests/registry_consistency.rs` makes drift a build failure. Resolved the gitbot-fleet/verisimdb 8080 collision (→ 9100 / 6475).
- **Reference provider + executable conformance (ADR 0002).** New `provider/` crate (`groove-provider`): dual-stack discovery, content-negotiated JSON/A2ML manifests, connect/heartbeat/disconnect lifecycle with linear handles, hash-chained attestation. `provider/tests/conformance.rs` implements one test per CONF-* ID.
- **Browser extension folded in (ADR 0005).** Moved from `groove-browser-harness` to `clients/browser-extension/`, remediated (MV2 permissions bug fixed, dual-stack probing, spec lifecycle, generated port table, real icons, removed the false "Idris2-verified" claim); shared logic in `clients/js/groove-client.js`.
- **Licensing normalized (ADR 0004):** MPL-2.0 code / CC-BY-SA-4.0 prose; stale AGPL/PMPL removed.
- **CI (ADR 0008):** real matrix — rust workspace tests, registry-drift guard, web-ext lint + extension tests, zig (allow-fail until first green), spec-consistency; plus allow-fail `proofs.yml`. Layout standard in `docs/REPO-LAYOUT.adoc`.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` → **30 passing** (registry consistency, validate golden tests, check-compat truth table, 11 conformance tests, probe integration, timefmt).
- Smoke-tested end to end: `groove-provider` + `groove probe` discovers `groove-ref` on `[::1]` and `127.0.0.1`; both encodings content-negotiate via curl; full connect → heartbeat(204) → disconnect(200) → re-disconnect(410) with a valid hash chain.
- Extension: `web-ext lint` 0 errors; `node --test` 8 passing; `validate_structure.sh` 9/9.
- Gates: no stray AGPL/PMPL outside `LICENSES/`; every CONF-* ID has a matching test; version coherent across Cargo.toml/SPEC/README.

## Owner follow-ups (out of scope for this PR)

- Merge the pointer PRs in `groove` and `groove-browser-harness`, then **archive both repos** on GitHub.
- Optional: rename `groove-protocol` → `groove` afterward for the cleaner name (ADR 0001; redirects preserved).
- The `zig` and `proofs` CI jobs are allow-fail until a runner with those toolchains proves them green.
